synthesis: Ordinary almost-periodic Jensen theory survives the source's generalized half-strip limit through the Jensen function itself: convergence of truncated logarithmic means produces a convex limiting Jensen function whose one-sided slopes still control argument motion and strip-zero frequency, with exact identities at differentiability points.
source_support: The ordinary theorem package identifies one-sided Jensen slopes with bounds on mean motions and slope differences with bounds on strip-zero frequencies. Theorems 1 and 2 retain Jensen convergence and convexity under inner-strip uniform convergence plus half-strip mean convergence, and the proof transfers truncated logarithmic means, suppresses horizontal boundary terms, and uses corrected convex finite-window means to recover the same slope bounds.
nonparaphrase_operation: Uses the convex Jensen function as a stable intermediate representation: analytic approximants are compressed to logarithmic means, and subgradient data of their limit is decoded as motion and zero-count information.
limits: The result requires nontrivial analytic functions, continuation on the stated half-strip, uniform convergence on an inner strip, mean convergence with positive index, and interior-strip control. Without differentiability the source gives one-sided inequalities rather than a unique motion or exact zero frequency; OCR makes some signs and constants unsafe.
quality_reason: The four parents supply complementary parts of one mechanism—ordinary slope semantics, the generalized convergence interface, the transfer theorem, and its truncation/convexity proof—so the synthesis is not obtainable from any single parent and does not rely on its broad title alone.

synthesis: The source turns vertical value statistics into zero statistics by representing the Jensen function of f-x as the logarithmic potential of the unweighted value law, then using the area theorem to identify the curvature of that potential with the continuous density of the |f'|^2-weighted value law; integrating this curvature across real parts gives strip-zero frequency.
source_support: The source separately constructs unweighted and derivative-weighted asymptotic value measures, obtains the logarithmic-potential formula by truncating the singular logarithm, and uses area counting plus Fubini to connect the weighted measure to preimage multiplicities. Under a jointly continuous weighted density it derives twice differentiability and the curvature identity. Theorems 13 and 14 instantiate the chain for log zeta and zeta, including mean motions and strip frequencies.
nonparaphrase_operation: Changes representation twice: vertical occupation becomes a planar logarithmic potential, while derivative weighting converts occupation into an area/preimage law. Differentiation and integration then translate between local curvature and stripwise zero counts.
limits: The pointwise curvature statement needs absolute continuity and joint continuity of the weighted density, and exact normalizations are OCR-sensitive. The log-zeta result is restricted to its branch domain; the zeta theorem has exceptional target behavior, notably x=0, and neither theorem localizes ordinary zeta zeros on the critical line.
quality_reason: The parents jointly establish every link—measure construction, singular-potential passage, area/preimage counting, regularity, and the zeta/log-zeta specialization—so this is a concrete cross-section mechanism rather than a thematic association.

synthesis: A chosen branch of log f can retain Jensen and argument-principle information despite horizontal cuts: cut-intersecting local windows form a mean-zero exceptional set, explicit loop variations repair the finite-window argument balance, and the averaged sum of those corrections vanishes, leaving the limiting Jensen-slope and zero-frequency relations unchanged.
source_support: The source defines cut-aware one-sided variations by continuation, endpoint limits, and subdivision. Zero frequency zero for f makes windows meeting cuts negligible in mean, while local Backlund-style estimates bound variations and cut contributions. It then adds loop terms around every cut to the vertical variations and their integrals to the finite-window Jensen mean; these restore the one-sided derivative identities, and the total correction tends uniformly to zero before Cauchy's theorem is passed to the limit.
nonparaphrase_operation: Represents monodromy as an explicit finite-scale defect term. Loop correction makes the cut-domain argument principle exact, and sparse-exception averaging removes that correction from the limiting observable.
limits: This is not a generic branch-independence result. It depends on the source's chosen horizontal cut geometry, zero relative frequency of zeros of the exponentiated function, zero-free exponential approximants, local nondegeneracy estimates, and uniform inner-strip convergence. Corrections vanish only after averaging, and exact orientations and constants are OCR-sensitive.
quality_reason: Distinct parents provide the branch construction, exceptional-set control, local variation estimates, and the vanishing loop repair. Together they support the asserted neutralization mechanism without claiming that cuts or monodromy disappear pointwise.

synthesis: Finite Euler products provide an exact first stage in which ordinary almost periodicity and prime-log equidistribution identify vertical value laws with Haar laws on a finite torus; generalized Jensen and characteristic-function stability then form a second stage that transfers those laws, Jensen functions, motions, and zero-frequency statements to zeta and the chosen branch of log zeta.
source_support: The partial products and logarithms are ordinary almost periodic and converge uniformly in the right half-plane, while cited mean-square convergence supplies the larger-half-plane approximation. Linear independence of the prime-log frequencies makes every continuous torus observable have the same Haar and long-vertical mean, exactly identifying finite torus and vertical distributions. Theorems 1–4 and their Fourier proofs then pass Jensen functions and unweighted value laws to the generalized limits, with a separate good/bad-window argument for logarithms.
nonparaphrase_operation: Separates exact finite phase algebra from analytic completion: equidistributed torus flow realizes independent prime phases, and Jensen functions plus characteristic functions are the stable interfaces through which the infinite zeta limit is taken.
limits: The passage uses both inner-strip uniform convergence and the stated half-strip mean convergence, as well as the specified branch domain for log zeta and an externally cited mean-square fact. Finite-dimensional equidistribution alone does not justify the infinite limit, and the source does not license extension beyond Re(s)>1/2.
quality_reason: The parents jointly connect finite products, torus equidistribution, generalized analytic convergence, Fourier stability, and branch control. No single parent supplies both the exact finite model and the justified infinite transfer.

synthesis: Product independence turns the unweighted characteristic function into a product of local factors and the derivative-weighted transform into sums of products with marked factors. Reserving sufficiently many small unmarked factors yields arbitrarily strong polynomial Fourier decay and smooth densities; the sharper reciprocal-radius conditions r_n^{-1}=O(n) and r_n^{-1}=o(n) yield fixed and arbitrarily strong exponential decay, respectively, giving real-analytic and entire density extensions.
source_support: Theorem 5 defines the unweighted and |g_n|^2-weighted torus pushforwards. Its proof factors the former into K_0 products and expands the latter with K_1/K_2 insertions, uses small-radius oscillatory bounds to allocate inverse powers of frequency, and uses S_0, S_1, and S_2 to pass to convergent limiting products and marked sums. Fourier inversion supplies smoothness, while Theorem 8 combines the reciprocal-radius budget with Stirling estimates to obtain exponential decay and the analytic/entire dichotomy.
nonparaphrase_operation: Treats Fourier decay as a factor budget: unmarked independent components purchase smoothing, while marked insertions preserve derivative information and consume additional summability. Quantitative component scales determine how much exponential decay remains after this allocation.
limits: Small radii and the theorem's nondegeneracy and summability hypotheses are essential. The weighted law needs the additional marked-factor sums and cannot be inferred from the unweighted product alone. Mere r_n to 0 yields finite-order smoothness for sufficiently long sums, not analyticity; exact indices, constants, and OCR-damaged series must not be reconstructed.
quality_reason: The six parents form a coherent proof chain from the Fourier criterion through finite factorization, infinite-product closure, spatial bounds, and the exact O(n)/o(n) radius thresholds. The accepted synthesis preserves those thresholds rather than replacing them with an unsupported geometric-rate claim.

synthesis: Strict positivity of the unweighted and derivative-weighted limiting densities is proved by different resources: divergent small component lengths give phase-polygon reachability and, through tail support plus convolution, positivity of the unweighted density; the weighted density additionally requires two regular phase preimages of the same value whose derivative-like weights stay separated, preventing simultaneous degeneration after a common tail is added.
source_support: For the unweighted law, the source uses linearized small circles and the polygon inequality to steer a finite phase block toward any target, proves that the remaining tail puts positive mass in every open neighborhood, and applies the limiting convolution formula to obtain F(x)>0. For the weighted law, it constructs two equal-value phase pairs with nonzero value-map Jacobians but different g_2 values, builds local inverse charts, and lower-bounds the sum of two squared weights by a positive multiple of an unweighted tail measure, whose already-positive density yields G(x)>0.
nonparaphrase_operation: Separates support controllability from fiber nondegeneracy: vector-sum geometry reaches values, convolution makes reachability robust, and redundant regular representations with separated marks turn that unweighted robustness into a lower bound for the weighted pushforward.
limits: Both arguments use sufficiently small analytic circular components and divergence of the effective radii. Weighted positivity also needs unequal radii, nonzero Jacobians, separated weights, and the previously established positive tail density. These are not general positivity theorems for arbitrary sums or arbitrary weighted pushforwards; exact Jacobians and constants are OCR-unsafe.
quality_reason: The two parents explicitly prove different positivity mechanisms and the second depends on the first. Their conjunction supports the claimed distinction and supplies a genuine dependency unavailable from either unit alone.

synthesis: Exponentiation transports the log-zeta distribution program to zeta by periodizing over every logarithmic lift and applying the change-of-variables Jacobian. The ordinary zeta density is |x|^{-2} times the lift sum of the log density, whereas derivative weighting compensates that factor; Gaussian control of the lift sums transfers smoothness and supports the later Jensen-curvature formulas while making x=0 and the multiplicity of logarithmic preimages essential features rather than removable notation.
source_support: Theorem 11 supplies smooth, decaying log-Euler densities. Theorem 12 pushes their measures through exp, states the distinct ordinary and derivative-weighted density formulas over all logarithms of x, defines both densities to be zero at x=0, and dominates the periodized derivative series. Theorems 13 and 14 then use these laws in logarithmic-potential, curvature, mean-motion, and zero-frequency formulas, with the zeta proof explicitly summing the log-zeta relations over logarithmic preimages.
nonparaphrase_operation: Uses the covering map exp as the bridge: periodization records its many sheets, the Jacobian distinguishes ordinary from derivative-weighted pushforwards, and decay of distant lifts makes regularity and potential-theoretic transfer legitimate.
limits: The density formulas are singularly expressed only for x nonzero and positivity is asserted only away from zero. Boundary vanishing transfers only with the explicit |x| powers stated in Theorem 12; the source warns that omitting them makes even bounded-set mass vanishing false. Exact derivative powers and some boundary symbols are OCR-sensitive.
quality_reason: The parents jointly connect the abstract log-density theorem, the many-sheeted pushforward, and both curvature theorems. This supports a concrete representation change and its singular limits, not merely the observation that zeta is the exponential of log zeta.

synthesis: At the Re(s)=1/2 boundary, divergence of the log-Euler square-sum forces the nonzero-frequency characteristic function to collapse and the unweighted log-value density to flatten uniformly while retaining total mass. The logarithmic-potential formulas nevertheless make the Jensen functions diverge there; their slope/zero-count consequences, accumulated over the whole permitted half-plane, yield N(T)/T tending to infinity for log zeta minus any target and for zeta minus a nonzero target.
source_support: Theorem 10 uses divergence of S_0 and the K_0 product estimate to force Fourier-transform decay on punctured frequency annuli, then dominated inversion gives uniform density flattening. Theorem 11 specializes this to log Euler factors at the half-plane boundary. Theorems 13 and 14 express the relevant Jensen functions as logarithmic potentials, prove their boundary divergence, and connect their slopes to zero frequencies; Theorem 15 explicitly records the resulting superlinear normalized cumulative zero counts over Re(s)>1/2.
nonparaphrase_operation: Contrasts two representations of the same spreading law: fixed-location density values vanish because mass disperses, while the unbounded logarithmic observable grows. Convex Jensen slopes then convert that boundary growth into cumulative zero abundance.
limits: The flattening statement concerns the unweighted log-value density and is not convergence of the probability measures to zero; frequency zero remains normalized. The zero conclusion is cumulative over the full half-plane, not divergence in every fixed narrower strip or localization on Re(s)=1/2. For zeta the target must be nonzero, and none of these statements proves the Riemann hypothesis.
quality_reason: All five parents are needed to support the chain from square-sum divergence through Fourier flattening and logarithmic-potential growth to the explicitly stated half-plane count. The synthesis corrects the title's possible ambiguity: it is characteristic-function collapse and density flattening, not collapse of the diverging variance itself.
